text:
jordan_infra: Heads-up — after last night's node upgrade in eu-west-1 we started seeing recurring NCCL timeouts and GPU contention spikes. P99 for infer pods jumped ~2.5x and some jobs hit OOM+nvml errors. We're rolling back drivers on a canary subset (10 nodes) now. Need quick consensus on a pin/rollback strategy and a short-term gate so we don't reintroduce the bad combo during next rollout.

sasha_sre: scope? all GPU instance types or just A100/RTX?

jordan_infra: Mainly A100s on the batch cluster (k8s-gpu-batch-eu). A subset of 48 nodes showed NCCL rank disconnects. Kernel on those nodes is 5.15.0-70, driver bumped to 540.x during automated update. Pre-upgrade had 535.54 which was stable.

mike_ops: Do we have capacity to drain+rollback the whole pool? If we cordon 48 nodes we may hit capacity constraints for realtime.

jordan_infra: We do not. That's why canary is 10 nodes first. If canary is green, we can do staged rollback 10->24->48 with manual throttle. But we need a policy to prevent the upgrade job from re-applying 540 on the remaining nodes.

lem_eng: Re: policy — recommend two things: 1) apt/dpkg hold on the driver package on the stable nodes, 2) add a version gate in our rollout job so it skips nodes with label gpu.driver.locked=true.

sasha_sre: Agreed. For 1) we'd use apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 or equivalent rpm command. For k8s side here's a quick helm value snippet we can flip to gate:```yaml
nodeSelector:
  gpu.driver.locked: "true"
tolerations: []
```

jordan_infra: Also propose adding a temporary matrix to devdocs listing validated (kernel, driver, cuda, nccl) combos. People keep assuming forward compatibility. Quick draft table I've pasted below:```text
validated combos (eu-west-1 batch cluster)
- kernel 5.15.0-70 | driver 535.54 | cuda 11.8 | nccl 2.14 -> OK
- kernel 5.15.0-70 | driver 540.42 | cuda 11.8 | nccl 2.14 -> FAIL (symm.rendezvous timeouts)
- kernel 6.1.0-10  | driver 540.42 | cuda 12.1 | nccl 2.15 -> OK
- kernel 6.1.0-10  | driver 535.54 | cuda 11.8 | nccl 2.14 -> OK (compat mode)
```

mike_ops: The matrix is useful. For immediate mitigation we should: 1) add apt hold 535 on current stable nodes, 2) prevent auto-upgrades by setting repo pin priority lower for 540, 3) cascade a canary rollback to the other 2 AZs but only if batch queue depth < X.

sasha_sre: On the hold command — caution: apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 will persist across reboots but not across a re-image. For autoscaling groups we must bake an AMI with the pinned driver or make startup script check for /etc/gpu-driver-locked. Suggest both: hold + baked AMI for now.

jordan_infra: Good point. I'll open a short-lived infra ticket to bake AMI with 535 pinned and update ASG launch_templates.

deploy-bot: rollback-job/1749201155 started -> rolling back driver to 535.54 on 10 nodes in k8s-gpu-batch-eu (canary). Job link: https://deploy.internal/rollback/1749201155

lem_eng: Tests to run on canary: small multi-GPU NCCL allreduce (4-way) with synthetic traffic, end-to-end inference p99 under 100ms target, and NVML leak check for 20m. If all pass, approve next stage. I'll add those to the job's post-checks.

sasha_sre: Also add a quick network test — some of the errors looked like flaky ethernet link negotiation after driver change. Run ethtool -S on ixgbe devices pre/post.

mike_ops: Cost note: if we stagger rollback across AZs, spare capacity dips and we may autoscale new nodes in us-east as fallback which increases inter-region egress costs for replication tasks. Prefer to keep within region if possible.

jordan_infra: Agreed. We'll throttle and aim for same-AZ replacements. If capacity falls below 10% spare, stop and notify.

lem_eng: For longer-term, propose a 'lockstep matrix' enforcement: release pipeline must pass canonical compatibility test matrix before enabling driver push. Add a stage that runs our small validation harness against a representative node image and only flips the repo tag if green. Also add a 'force-allow' with explicit oncall approval for emergency hotfixes.

sasha_sre: That plus a package holdlist for each fleet would have prevented this. Let's export current stable list and commit to infra-config repo. Also add a scheduled weekly dry-run of the matrix tests.

mike_ops: One more operational item: update oncall runbook to include commands to quickly snapshot current driver state:```bash
dpkg -l | grep nvidia
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv
apt-mark showhold | grep nvidia || true
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
```

jordan_infra: I'll update the runbook and link to the deploy job and matrix doc. After canary finishes (ETA ~15m) I'll post results here.

deploy-bot: rollback-job/1749201155 progress: 10/10 nodes rolled back, post-checks queued.

jordan_infra: Canary post-checks passed (ncc-l small allreduce ok, nvml stable, p99 restored). Proceeding to stage 2 (24 nodes). Throttle at 4 nodes/min.

lem_eng: Thumbs up. I'm patching the rollout job to skip nodes with label gpu.driver.locked=true and adding the apt hold code to the bake step.

sasha_sre: I'll draft the short-lived gating policy and a PR to infra-config with the holdlist. After that we can close the incident and schedule the matrix enforcement rollout.

mike_ops: Keep me posted on capacity; if stage 2 trips autoscaling, we'll pause and re-evaluate.

jordan_infra: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

(incident-note: added to postmortem tracker under INC-174920; linking matrix doc once PR merges)
